column1: arrogance§His arrogance cost the team the contract: he corrected the client's pronunciation of her own company's name.§他的**傲慢**让团队丢了合同——他纠正客户对自家公司名字的发音。§ar-（向）+ rog（要求，同 interrogate 审问）→ 向人索取尊重
arrogant§The letter is arrogant in a way its writer clearly cannot hear, assuming agreement before offering a single reason.§这封信**傲慢**得连写信人自己显然都听不出来——一条理由未给，就先假定别人会同意。§
articulate§Few witnesses were as articulate as the janitor, who laid out the sequence of events in eight clear sentences.§没几个证人像那位清洁工那样**表达清晰**，他用八个明白的句子把事情的先后讲了个透。§art（关节／技艺，同 article 条款）→ 一节一节说清楚
articulation§The articulation between the two policies is missing: each makes sense alone, and together they require the impossible.§两项政策之间缺少**衔接**——各自成立，合起来却要求做到不可能的事。§

artifice§The painting's depth is pure artifice: flat pigment, a vanishing point, and three centuries of practice at fooling the eye.§这幅画的纵深纯属**巧技**——平涂的颜料、一个灭点，加上三百年骗眼睛的功夫。§art（技艺）+ fic（做，同 factory 工厂）
artistic§Her objection was artistic, not commercial: she thought the cover was ugly and said so to a room of accountants.§她的反对是**艺术上的**而非商业上的——她认为封面丑，并当着满屋会计说了出来。§
artistry§The artistry lies in the restraint: the whole score uses four instruments, and never more than two at once.§**艺术功力**体现在克制上——整部配乐只用四件乐器，而且从不同时超过两件。§
ascertain§Investigators could not ascertain the time of the failure, because the only clock in the room had stopped weeks earlier.§调查人员无法**确定**故障发生的时间，因为屋里唯一的钟几周前就停了。§as-（向）+ certain（确定）→ 弄确定
ascetic§The ascetic slept on boards and ate once a day, and pilgrims walked three hundred miles to watch him do it.§这位**苦行者**睡木板、日食一餐，朝圣者步行三百英里去看他这样生活。§askē（修炼）→ 训练自己
asceticism§Asceticism appealed to him less as faith than as engineering: he wanted to know how little a body actually required.§**苦行主义**吸引他的与其说是信仰，不如说是工程学——他想知道身体究竟需要多少就够。§
aspersion§He cast an aspersion on her research without naming a single paper, which made the charge impossible to answer.§他对她的研究泼了一句**中伤**，却一篇论文都没点名，让这指控无从回应。§a-（向）+ spers（撒，同 disperse 散开）→ 泼过去
assault§The assault on the ridge began before dawn and cost more men in twenty minutes than the previous month had.§对山脊的**强攻**在黎明前打响，二十分钟的伤亡超过此前整整一个月。§as-（向）+ salt ← sal（跳，同 salient 突出的）→ 扑上去

assiduous§An assiduous editor, she checked every citation in a four-hundred-page manuscript and found eleven that led nowhere.§作为一位**勤勉的**编辑，她核对了四百页手稿里的每条引文，找出十一条查无出处。§as-（向）+ sid（坐，同 reside 居住）→ 一直坐在那儿做

assimilation§Assimilation cost the community its language in two generations, and the third is now paying tutors to get it back.§**同化**在两代人里夺走了这个社群的语言，第三代如今正花钱请老师学回来。§as-（向）+ simil（相似，同 similar 相似的）→ 变得跟别人一样
assure§She assured the board that the deadline was safe, and then quietly moved three people off other projects to make it so.§她向董事会**保证**期限没问题，随后悄悄把三个人从别的项目调过来，好让它真没问题。§as-（向）+ sure（确定）
astute§An astute reader will notice that the report never states the number outright, only the direction it moved.§**精明的**读者会注意到，这份报告从未直接给出数字，只说了它变动的方向。§astut（机敏）
attenuate§Distance attenuates the signal, so a station audible in the next town is pure static forty miles out.§距离会**削弱**信号，所以隔壁镇能听清的电台，四十英里外就只剩杂音。§at-（向）+ tenu（薄，同 tenuous 纤细的）→ 变薄变细

attribution§The attribution to Rembrandt was withdrawn in 1968, and the painting's value fell by ninety-eight percent overnight.§1968 年这幅画对伦勃朗的**归属认定**被撤销，画价一夜跌去百分之九十八。§at-（向）+ tribut（分派，同 tribute 贡品）→ 归到某人名下
atypical§The symptoms were atypical enough that three doctors missed the diagnosis before a fourth thought to ask about her travel.§症状**非典型**到三位医生都误诊了，直到第四位想到问她的旅行史。§a-（不）+ typical（典型的）
audacious§The plan was audacious to the point of absurdity: eleven men, one truck, and a bank in the middle of a garrison town.§这个计划**大胆**到荒唐——十一个人、一辆卡车，外加驻军小镇正中的一家银行。§aud（大胆）
augment§The city augmented its water supply with a single reservoir, and that one decision carried it through the next two droughts.§这座城市靠一座水库**增补**了供水，仅此一项决定就让它熬过了随后两次旱情。§aug（增加，同 auction 拍卖／增价）
aural§The evidence was aural, not visual: nobody saw the crash, but four households heard it and agreed on the time.§证据是**听觉上的**而非视觉上的——没人看见撞击，但四户人家听见了，且对时间说法一致。§aur（耳朵）

auspicious§The opening was hardly auspicious: the projector failed, the guest of honor arrived late, and it rained through the reception.§开幕算不上**吉利**——投影坏了，主宾迟到，招待会全程下雨。§au（鸟）+ spic（看，同 inspect 检查）→ 古罗马看飞鸟占卜吉凶
austere§The chapel is austere by design: white walls, wooden benches, and one window placed exactly where the morning sun enters.§这座礼拜堂**朴素**是有意为之——白墙、木凳，一扇窗恰好开在晨光射入的位置。§austēr（干涩）
austerity§Years of austerity closed the libraries first, and the town is still arguing about what that cost the children who grew up meanwhile.§多年的**紧缩**最先关掉的是图书馆，这座镇子至今仍在争论那让期间长大的孩子付出了什么。§

authenticate§Three laboratories authenticated the letter, and only the fourth noticed that the paper contained a bleach unknown before 1954.§三家实验室**鉴定**这封信为真，只有第四家注意到纸里含有 1954 年前不存在的漂白剂。§authent（真的，同 author 作者）
authoritarian§The reforms were authoritarian in method and popular in result, which is why historians still cannot agree how to judge them.§这些改革手段**独裁**、结果得民心，所以史学家至今无法就如何评判它们达成一致。§

autocrat§The autocrat kept no minutes and made no appointments he could not reverse, so nothing outlived his personal attention.§这位**独裁者**不留会议记录，也不做无法撤销的任命，因此没有任何事能脱离他本人的注意而存续。§auto（自己）+ crat（统治，同 democrat 民主派）
autocratic§His autocratic style worked while the company was twelve people and failed the moment it reached two hundred.§他**专断的**作风在公司只有十二人时管用，一到两百人就失灵了。§

autonomy§The region won autonomy over schools and courts but not over taxes, which left it responsible for everything and funded for nothing.§该地区赢得了学校与法院的**自治权**，税收却没有，结果它样样都得管，样样都没钱。§auto（自己）+ nom（法则，同 economy 经济）→ 自己立规矩
avant-garde§The avant-garde of 1913 is the museum wall of today, which is roughly what happens to every avant-garde eventually.§1913 年的**先锋派**成了今天的美术馆展墙，每一代先锋派最终大抵如此。§
avarice§Avarice, not need, drove the second round of layoffs: the company had just posted its most profitable quarter on record.§驱动第二轮裁员的是**贪婪**而非需要——公司刚公布了有记录以来最赚钱的一个季度。§avar（贪）
averse§She is not averse to risk; she is averse to risk that nobody has bothered to measure.§她并不**反感**风险，她反感的是没人肯去衡量的风险。§a-（离开）+ vers（转，同 reverse 倒转）→ 转身走开
aversion§His aversion to flying cost him two promotions and gained him a remarkable knowledge of European railway timetables.§他对飞行的**厌恶**让他丢了两次升职，却换来对欧洲铁路时刻表惊人的熟悉。§
avert§A single phone call averted the strike, though nobody outside the room ever learned what was promised on it.§一通电话就**避免**了罢工，尽管屋外没人知道电话里承诺了什么。§a-（离开）+ vert（转，同 convert 转变）→ 把事转开
avid§An avid reader of shipping schedules, he could tell you which port a container had cleared and when it would arrive.§作为船期表的**狂热**读者，他能告诉你某个集装箱在哪个港口放行、何时到岸。§avid（渴求）

avocation§Beekeeping began as an avocation and slowly took over: he now keeps four hundred hives and teaches accounting part-time.§养蜂起初只是**副业嗜好**，后来慢慢反客为主——他如今养四百箱蜂，兼职教会计。§a-（离开）+ voc（召唤，同 vocation 天职）→ 主业之外的召唤
avoidance§Tax avoidance is legal and tax evasion is not, and the whole industry lives in the two inches between them.§避税**规避**合法，逃税不合法，整个行业就活在这两者之间的方寸之地。§
avuncular§His avuncular manner put students at ease, though anyone who mistook it for softness discovered otherwise at the oral exam.§他**长辈般亲切**的做派让学生放松，但谁要把这当成好说话，口试时就会发现不然。§avuncul（舅舅）
awaken§The report awakened a public that had ignored twenty earlier warnings, mostly because this one had photographs.§这份报告**唤醒**了此前无视二十次警告的公众，主要因为这一次配了照片。§
backfire§The advertisement backfired badly: within a day the slogan was a joke, and sales fell in every market that had seen it.§这则广告**适得其反**——一天之内标语成了笑柄，凡是投放过的市场销量都下滑。§
backlash§The backlash against the new rules was fiercer than the rules themselves warranted, and the council withdrew them within a month.§对新规的**强烈反弹**远超新规本身应得的程度，市议会一个月内就撤回了它们。§
ballad§The ballad tells the whole story in nine verses, and every version collected since 1780 keeps the same three details.§这首**叙事歌谣**用九节唱完整个故事，1780 年以来采集到的每个版本都保留着同样三个细节。§
banal§The speech was banal in the specific way that committee writing always is: every sentence true, no sentence necessary.§这篇讲稿**平庸**得很有委员会文风的特色——每句都对，没有一句是必要的。§
banality§What frightened her was the banality of it: the orders were typed on ordinary paper and filed like invoices.§让她害怕的正是其**平庸无奇**——命令用普通纸打印，像发票一样归档。§
bane§Damp was the bane of the collection: it destroyed more manuscripts in forty years than fire, theft, and war combined.§潮湿是这批藏品的**祸根**，四十年里毁掉的手稿比火灾、盗窃和战争加起来还多。§
baneful§The baneful effects of the drainage scheme appeared a decade later, when the wells the village depended on ran dry.§这项排水工程的**有害**后果十年后才显现——全村赖以为生的水井干涸了。§

bankrupt§The firm went bankrupt owing money to three hundred suppliers, most of them small workshops that never recovered.§这家公司**破产**时欠着三百家供应商的钱，其中多数是再没缓过来的小作坊。§banc（长凳）+ rupt（断裂，同 rupture 破裂）→ 钱庄的凳子被砸断
banter§Their banter looked friendly to outsiders, but each remark landed on a sore point both of them had agreed never to name.§他们的**戏谑**在外人看来是友好的，可每句话都戳在两人默契地从不提及的痛处。§
baroque§The design is baroque to the point of exhaustion: every surface carved, every corner gilded, nowhere for the eye to rest.§这个设计**巴洛克式**繁复到令人疲惫——处处雕花、角角贴金，眼睛无处可歇。§
barrage§A barrage of questions from the floor kept the minister at the podium for ninety minutes past his scheduled departure.§台下**连珠炮般的**提问把这位大臣留在讲台上，比预定离场晚了九十分钟。§
barter§The two villages bartered salt for wool for six centuries, and neither used coined money until the railway arrived.§这两个村子以盐**易**羊毛六百年，直到铁路修通才开始用铸币。§
beautify§Money meant to beautify the square bought eleven planters and a fountain that has never once been switched on.§用来**美化**广场的钱买了十一个花坛和一座从没开过的喷泉。§
bedazzle§The demonstration bedazzled the investors, who wrote checks before anyone asked what the machine actually did.§这场演示**迷惑**了投资人，他们还没人问清那机器究竟做什么就开了支票。§be-（使）+ dazzle（眩目）
beguile§His easy manner beguiled the committee for two years, until an intern checked the credentials nobody had thought to verify.§他随和的做派**蒙骗**了委员会两年，直到一名实习生去查了那份没人想到要核实的履历。§be-（使）+ guile（诡计）
behavior§The behavior changed only when the fee changed: nothing the campaign said moved a single household, and two cents did.§**行为**只在收费变化时才改变——宣传说什么都撼动不了一户人家，两分钱却做到了。§
belated§The belated apology arrived after the family had moved, changed lawyers, and stopped expecting one at all.§这份**迟来的**道歉送到时，那家人已经搬走、换了律师，也早就不指望了。§be-（使）+ late（晚）
belie§His cheerful email belies the state of the project: three deadlines have passed and the prototype still will not start.§他那封轻快的邮件**掩盖了**项目的真实状况——三个期限已过，样机仍然启动不了。§be-（关于）+ lie（说谎）→ 把真相说反
belittle§Reviewers belittled the discovery for a decade, and the same journals now describe it as a turning point.§评论者**贬低**了这项发现十年，如今同样的期刊把它称作转折点。§be-（使）+ little（小）
bellicose§The speech was bellicose enough that two embassies asked, privately, whether it represented actual policy.§这篇讲话**好战**到有两个使馆私下询问，它是否代表真实政策。§bell（战争，同 rebel 反叛）

belligerence§Her belligerence in negotiations won small points and lost the relationship that would have delivered the large ones.§她在谈判中的**好斗**赢了些小分，却输掉了本可换来大局的那层关系。§bell（战争）+ ger（进行，同 gesture 举动）→ 打起来
benefactor§An anonymous benefactor paid the school's heating bills for eleven winters, and the trustees never learned who it was.§一位匿名的**捐助者**为这所学校付了十一个冬天的取暖费，董事会始终不知道是谁。§bene（好）+ fac（做，同 factory 工厂）
beneficial§The delay proved beneficial: two months of extra testing caught a flaw that would have cost far more after launch.§这次延期反倒**有益**——多出的两个月测试逮到一处缺陷，上线后再发现代价要大得多。§
beneficiary§The chief beneficiary of the reform was not the tenants it named but the agencies hired to administer it.§这项改革最大的**受益者**不是它写明的租户，而是被雇来执行它的那些机构。§
benefit§The benefit is real but narrow: the drug helps one patient in nine, and nobody can yet predict which one.§这项**益处**真实但有限——药物对九个病人里的一个有效，而目前无人能预测是哪一个。§
benevolent§The landlord's benevolent reputation rested on one famous gesture and forty years of quietly raising the rent.§这位房东**仁慈**的名声建立在一次著名的善举，和四十年悄悄涨租之上。§bene（好）+ vol（意愿，同 volunteer 志愿者）→ 心存善意
benign§The growth turned out to be benign, but the six days of waiting rearranged how she thought about the next twenty years.§肿块最终是**良性的**，可那六天的等待重塑了她对往后二十年的想法。§ben（好，同 benefit 益处）
